findings.detail: Delivery advances only a per-subscriber timestamp after send_message; retries, concurrent loops, and partial failures have no durable article/subscriber attempt or idempotency key, allowing duplicates or skips.

Ingestion stores source URL and local created_at but no fetched_at, source publication time, license/attribution, content hash, freshness bound, or provenance policy; duplicate handling is URL-hash only.
start/stop directly toggle chat_id state; schema has no consent version, request receipt, deletion/retention policy, audit event, or operator reconciliation.
callback-handler.service independently polls Telegram with the same class of bearer token and sends replies; no deduplication, delivery receipt, rate limit, or lifecycle linkage is evidenced.
Units run as root and load token/database configuration from environment/.env; sandboxing, least privilege, and secret rotation/ownership evidence are absent.
Per-article send exceptions are printed and skipped while the loop continues; no bounded retry/dead-letter/alert or customer-visible failure state exists.
publish_news.py and legacy news_bot.py send directly to Telegram outside the subscription/outbox path, creating separate cursor, token, and audit boundaries.

knownBlockers: production key registry/trusted time/revocation/replay controls not established
interpretation: This is a read-only inventory and rejection of acceptance. It grants no delivery, deployment, Telegram, provider, customer, writer, or production authority. E0.3 remains first unmet and BLOCKED_OWNER; E0.4 remains non-production IN_PROGRESS.
